I farm here in the North West, and my maize plot is small — less than a quarter hectare — but the soil is tired like everybody's around here. Last season I put one bag of NPK 15-15-15 and a little urea at top-dress, and the cobs came out fair, so I will do the same again if the subsidy fertilizer reaches our ward in time. I cannot afford improved seed every year, but my brother-in-law gave me some Sammaz grains he saved from his own field, so I will plant that and intercrop with cowpea like I always do. I do not have a borehole or pump, so I wait for the rains; I weed myself with my wife and my two older children, and I will only call one or two young men from the village for a day or two when the weeding gets heavy.
